title: The Strange Case Of Dr. Jekyll And Mr.

facts: The eBook edition of *The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde* was originally released on June 27, 2008.
The most recent update of the eBook was on May 12, 2026.
The novella is divided into ten chapters.
The work is available for free under Project Gutenberg's licensing terms.
Mr. Utterson takes a Sunday walk with his kinsman Richard Enfield.
Hyde trampled a young girl and was forced to pay nearly one hundred pounds in compensation.
Hyde used a key to access a building behind a neglected door.
Utterson knows the identity of the check's drawer and is troubled by it.
Mr. Utterson is a lawyer who becomes troubled after reviewing Dr. Jekyll's will.
Dr. Jekyll's will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde.
Utterson learns from Dr. Lanyon that he has not seen Jekyll in over a decade.
Utterson discovers that Hyde has a key and free access to Jekyll's laboratory.
Mr. Utterson discusses Dr. Jekyll's will during a dinner at Jekyll's home.
Dr. Jekyll's will benefits Edward Hyde.
Jekyll becomes distressed when Utterson expresses concern about Hyde's behavior.
Jekyll asks Utterson to protect Hyde's interests if something happens to him.
Sir Danvers Carew was brutally murdered in October.
Mr. Hyde attacked and killed Carew using a heavy cane.
Mr. Utterson identified the victim and recognized the broken cane.
Hyde's residence was found ransacked with burned papers and the other half of the cane.
Utterson visits Dr. Jekyll at his laboratory after the murder of Sir Danvers Carew.
Jekyll receives a letter from Edward Hyde regarding his safety and escape.
The letter was delivered through the laboratory door, not by post.
Guest discovers that the letter's handwriting resembles Dr. Jekyll's own handwriting.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered.
Dr. Lanyon was mortally ill and refused to mention Jekyll.
Jekyll withdrew from society around January 12th.
Utterson received a sealed envelope from Lanyon to open only upon Jekyll's death or disappearance.
Mr. Utterson expresses concern about Dr. Jekyll during a Sunday walk.
Jekyll appears dejected and reluctant to join Utterson and Enfield.
Jekyll displays an expression of profound terror and despair before slamming the window shut.
Utterson and Enfield leave feeling deeply shaken and visibly disturbed.
Butler Poole alerts lawyer Utterson to a crisis at Dr. Jekyll's house.
Jekyll has been locked in his cabinet for a week.
Utterson and Poole discover Edward Hyde's poisoned corpse in Jekyll's cabinet.
Jekyll's new will names Utterson as the beneficiary.
Dr. Lanyon receives a letter from Dr. Henry Jekyll requesting the retrieval of a locked drawer.
The drawer contains powders, a blood-red phial, and a notebook related to chemical experiments.
A grotesque stranger arrives at midnight to collect the drawer and drinks a mixture that transforms him.
Lanyon learns that the creature who visited him was Mr. Hyde, the murderer of Carew.
Dr. Jekyll creates a drug that physically separates his good and evil aspects.
Jekyll initially alternates between his forms at will.
Jekyll commits murder while in the form of Edward Hyde.
Jekyll realizes he cannot prevent his permanent transformation into Hyde.
